title: Human Metapneumovirus–associated Infections Among American Indian and Alaska Native Children, 2019–2024

analysis.research_question_and_background: Data on human metapneumovirus (HMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) children are lacking publications.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted active ARI surveillance among hospitalized and outpatient AI/AN children <5 years of age at select facilities in Navajo Nation, White Mountain Apache Tribal lands, and Alaska (Anchorage and Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta).
analysis.methods: Children meeting a symptom-based ARI case definition from November 2019 to May 2024 were eligible. Data were collected via questionnaire and chart review. Mid-turbinate nasal swabs were tested for HMPV and other respiratory pathogens by polymerase chain reaction. Incidence rates of HMPV-associated hospitalization were calculated using Poisson regression. Seasonality was described, and risk factors for HMPV-associated hospitalization were assessed using Poisson multivariable modeling with robust standard errors.
analysis.main_results: Overall, 13.0% (218/1683) of children hospitalized with ARI and 7.0% (81/1165) of outpatient children with ARI were HMPV-positive. HMPV generally circulated December through May; seasonality and incidence were disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. In the Poisson model, age <2 years (adjusted risk ratio: 1.43 [1.08-1.90]) and presenting to care ≥4 days after illness onset (1.38 [1.09-1.75]) were significantly associated with increased risk for HMPV-associated hospitalization compared with HMPV-associated outpatient visits.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This analysis documents the burden of HMPV-associated ARI and hospitalization among AI/AN children <5 years of age as a baseline to inform the use of future pediatric HMPV prevention products.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide a baseline for understanding the burden of HMPV-associated ARI and hospitalization among AI/AN children, which can inform the development and implementation of future pediatric HMPV prevention products.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on specific tribal and geographic locations, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the observational nature of the study and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the lack of data on human metapneumovirus (HMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) children. Active ARI surveillance was conducted among hospitalized and outpatient AI/AN children under 5 years of age in Navajo Nation, White Mountain Apache Tribal lands, and Alaska from November 2019 to May 2024. Data were collected via questionnaires and chart reviews, with nasal swabs tested for HMPV and other respiratory pathogens using polymerase chain reaction. Incidence rates were calculated using Poisson regression, and seasonality and risk factors were assessed with multivariable modeling. Results showed that 13.0% of hospitalized children and 7.0% of outpatient children were HMPV-positive, with seasonality disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. Age <2 years and delayed care were significantly associated with increased risk of HMPV-associated hospitalization. The authors concluded that these findings serve as a baseline for future pediatric HMPV prevention strategies. The study's limitations include its focus on specific locations, which may limit generalizability, and its observational design, which may introduce confounding factors. The evidence is moderate in strength.

title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes acute lower respiratory infections, primarily affecting young children and older adults, with seasonal outbreaks peaking annually in March or April in the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. However, the factors driving HMPV seasonality in the United States remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases and age-specific emergency department visits across 10 US regions, fitting an age-stratified dynamic transmission model to assess spatiotemporal patterns and investigate the influence of environmental variables and viral interference from RSV on HMPV transmission rates.
analysis.methods: The study used an age-stratified dynamic transmission model to assess spatiotemporal patterns and investigate the influence of environmental variables and viral interference from RSV on HMPV transmission rates.
analysis.main_results: We found that models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all regions. Instead, HMPV timing was associated with RSV activity, with the HMPV transmission rate reduced in the presence of RSV. We showed that among the candidate models considered, only the models that included an RSV-associated term could reproduce the biennial pattern of HMPV observed in some regions, characterized by alternating “late-small” and “early-large” epidemics.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HMPV timing is associated with RSV activity, and that RSV interventions are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity despite reducing competition from RSV.

title: A one-step multiplex real-time reverse transcription quantitative PCR assay for rapid and simultaneous detection of human parainfluenza virus, human metapneumovirus, and rhinovirus in patients with acute respiratory tract infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: Acute respiratory tract infections caused by human parainfluenza virus, human metapneumovirus, and human rhinoviruses are often indistinguishable due to overlapping symptoms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay was established for simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV in clinical specimens. The study aimed to develop a method for rapid and accurate detection of these viruses in patients with acute respiratory tract infection.
analysis.methods: Primers and probes targeted conserved genomic regions, and an internal reference gene (B2M) was included for quality assurance. The limit of detection was determined via serial dilution of standard strains. Assay specificity was verified using 14 non-target pathogens, and repeatability was evaluated across various specimen concentrations. Clinical validation involved comparison with a commercial kit, with sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, agreement rate, and Kappa coefficient calculated for assessment.
analysis.main_results: The assay demonstrated a detection limit of 100 copies/mL for all three targets, expressed as the equivalent concentration in the original specimen before nucleic acid extraction. No cross-reactivity was observed against the 14 specified non-target pathogens under the conditions evaluated, and all eight target strains were detected. Repeatability testing showed coefficients of variation (CV) of ≤ 2% for Ct values at low and medium concentrations. At the individual-target level, the sensitivity of the developed assay was 98.82% for HRV, 98.55% for PIV, and 100.0% for MPV, with specificity of 100.0% for all three targets.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The method provides a technical approach for the simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV species A and B. Its clinical utility relative to comprehensive respiratory pathogen panels remains to be established.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of rapid diagnostic tools for respiratory infections caused by human metapneumovirus, human parainfluenza virus, and human rhinoviruses, improving clinical management and public health surveillance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not evaluate the method's performance in a broader range of clinical specimens or compare it directly to other diagnostic methods, which limits the generalisability of the findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited scope of the evaluation.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay for the simultaneous detection of human parainfluenza virus (PIV), human metapneumovirus (MPV), and human rhinoviruses (HRV) in patients with acute respiratory tract infections. The assay was designed to target conserved genomic regions and included an internal reference gene for quality assurance. It demonstrated a detection limit of 100 copies/mL for all three targets, with no cross-reactivity observed against 14 non-target pathogens. The method showed high sensitivity and specificity for each target, with pooled sensitivity and specificity of 99.06% and 100.0%, respectively, and an overall agreement rate of 99.24% with a commercial kit. The authors concluded that the method provides a technical approach for simultaneous detection of these viruses but noted that its clinical utility relative to comprehensive respiratory pathogen panels remains to be established. The study's limitations include the lack of broader clinical specimen evaluation and direct comparison with other diagnostic methods, which restricts the generalisability of the findings.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge of parents of school-going children aged 6-12 years regarding human metapneumovirus and to determine the effectiveness of a planned teaching programme in improving this knowledge. analysis.study_design_and_population: A pre-experimental one-group pretest and post-test design was employed in a selected community area. The study involved 100 parents of school-going children aged 6-12 years, with a focus on assessing their knowledge levels before and after the intervention.
analysis.methods: The study used a quantitative research design with non-probability convenient sampling. Data were collected using socio-demographic data sheets and structured knowledge questionnaires. Consent was obtained from all participants, and the study was conducted in a selected community area.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study used a non-probability sampling method, which may limit the generalizability of the results. Data were collected using socio-demographic data sheets and structured knowledge questionnaires. The pre-test results showed that 59% of participants had average knowledge scores, while the post-test results indicated an improvement, with 57% having good scores and 27% having very good scores. The study found no significant association between post-test knowledge scores and most demographic variables, except for the education level of the parents. title: Temporal dynamics of respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients in Shanghai, 2019–2023: a multi-center longitudinal surveillance study

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to explore the temporal patterns of common respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients before, during, and after the pandemic, as the epidemiology of SARI was greatly reshaped by COVID-19, yet long-term shifts in multi-pathogen circulation remain poorly characterized.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective multi-center observational study was conducted across seven sentinel hospitals in Shanghai, China, from 2019 to 2023, enrolling a total of 4738 participants aged ≥ 15 years.
analysis.methods: Hospitalized adult SARI patients were tested for 12 respiratory pathogens (22 subtypes) using real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR).
analysis.main_results: The overall pathogen detection rate decreased from 30.26% in the pre-pandemic period (2019) to 16.50% during the pandemic (2020–2022), then rebounded to 20.07% in the post-pandemic period (2023) (P < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A novel classification of four distinct temporal trends was established, including a transient peak for human metapneumovirus (HMPV).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Persistent multi-pathogen surveillance is required to guard against single-pathogen outbreaks and concurrent multi-pathogen epidemics, as respiratory pathogen circulation patterns changed substantially from 2019 to 2023.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is observational and retrospective, which may introduce bias and limit causal inference, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and comprehensive pathogen testing.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the temporal dynamics of respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients in Shanghai from 2019 to 2023. It found that the overall pathogen detection rate decreased during the pandemic but rebounded in the post-pandemic period. A novel classification of four distinct temporal trends was established, including a transient peak for human metapneumovirus (HMPV). The findings highlight the need for persistent multi-pathogen surveillance to monitor shifts in pathogen circulation and prevent outbreaks. The study's design, while observational, is supported by a large sample size and comprehensive testing, providing moderate confidence in its conclusions.

title: Incidence, shedding, and transmission of common respiratory viruses: data from a prospective, longitudinal, household cohort study in the Gambia from March 2021-June 2022.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory viruses are a major cause of morbidity in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet little is known about their incidence, risk factors, and transmission dynamics in community settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a prospective household cohort study in a peri-urban region of the Gambia. Households with ≥5 members, including at least one adult and one child, were enrolled and followed for one year.
analysis.methods: Upper respiratory tract swabs were collected weekly, regardless of symptoms, and tested by RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, seasonal coronaviruses, human rhinovirus (HRV), influenza A/B, RSV A/B, parainfluenza viruses 1-4, human metapneumovirus, and adenovirus. We estimated incidence, symptomatic fraction, shedding duration, and household secondary attack rates (SARs), and explored associations with virus type and demographic variables.
analysis.main_results: From 2 March 2021 to 13 June 2022, 349 participants from 52 households completed 14,421 scheduled and 129 unscheduled visits. Respiratory viruses were detected in 11.1% of visits (n = 1611), representing 1423 infection episodes. HRV was most common, infecting 86.5% of participants (2.4 infections per person-year). Children aged <5 and 5-17 years shed virus for longer than adults (p = 0.0005), with longer shedding durations seen for HRV and SARS-CoV-2. Overall, 88.4% of infections were asymptomatic, with the highest symptomatic proportions for SARS-CoV-2 (16.3%) and RSV (17.7%) (p = 0.03).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A large burden of asymptomatic infections underlies the circulation of respiratory viruses within households, with key differences in incidence, shedding and transmission across viral species.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance strategies and risk assessment for respiratory viruses in community settings, particularly highlighting the role of asymptomatic infections in household transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a single peri-urban region of the Gambia, limiting generalisability. The evidence is strong as it is based on a large sample size and comprehensive data collection.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the incidence, shedding, and transmission of respiratory viruses in a household cohort in the Gambia from March 2021 to June 2022. It highlights the significant role of asymptomatic infections in virus circulation and identifies differences in shedding and transmission across viral species. The research provides important insights into the epidemiology of respiratory viruses, particularly human metapneumovirus, in community settings, which can inform public health strategies. However, the study's focus on a single region may limit its generalisability. The evidence is strong due to the large sample size and systematic data collection methods.
